chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Suleiman al-Amiri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was ascended, the prayer was revealed as ten rak'at, two by two. So when Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn were born, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) increased seven rak'at as gratitude to Allah. So Allah permitted that for him, and he left Al-Fajr (prayer) as it was, not increasing in it due to the narrowness of its time, because it is attended by the angels of the night and the angels of the day.

So when Allah commanded him to shorten (the prayer) during travel, he removed six rak'at for his community, and left Al-Maghrib as it was, not reducing anything from it; and rather, the omission applies to whatever the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) had increased.
Thus, whoever doubts the original obligation in the first two rak'at, should face (continue) his prayer.
ai.seo_question: What is the origin and legal ruling of the five daily prayers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia perspective on the fluidity of prayer units, attributing the initial ten rak'at to the Mi'raj and a subsequent increase to the birth of the Imams, before settling into the current five. It clarifies that the extra units are supererogatory (nafl), meaning doubt in the core obligatory two rak'at does not invalidate the prayer, a nuance distinct from some Sunni juristic views. The text also notes the unique status of Fajr, where the overlap of night and day angels prevents any reduction, emphasizing the spiritual significance of dawn prayers.
